blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — central-line infection prevention
stem: Which bundle of practices is supported by CDC guidance for reducing central-line bloodstream-infection risk?

options.A: Use maximal sterile barriers for insertion, appropriate chlorhexidine-alcohol skin antisepsis, aseptic catheter care, and prompt removal when no longer essential.
options.B: Use sterile barriers for insertion, apply antibiotic ointment routinely at the site, and replace each central line every 24 hours to limit microbial growth.
options.C: Use chlorhexidine skin antisepsis for insertion, then keep the catheter through discharge when possible to avoid infection risk from another insertion.
options.D: Use hand hygiene and aseptic care, but omit maximal sterile barriers when the insertion site is clean and schedule routine central-line replacement every 48 hours.

rationale: A is correct. Current CDC guidance recommends maximal sterile barrier precautions for CVC/PICC insertion, preparation of clean skin with a greater-than-0.5% chlorhexidine preparation with alcohol before central venous catheter insertion when not contraindicated, aseptic technique for insertion and care, and prompt removal of any intravascular catheter that is no longer essential. B is incorrect because routine topical antibiotic ointment is not recommended for ordinary central-line insertion sites and routine CVC replacement to prevent infection is not recommended. C incorrectly retains an unnecessary catheter. D omits required maximal sterile barriers and introduces unsupported routine replacement.
educational_objective: Apply CDC-supported central-line infection-prevention practices: maximal sterile barriers, appropriate chlorhexidine-alcohol skin antisepsis, aseptic care, and prompt removal when the catheter is no longer essential.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Summary of Recommendations — Guidelines for the Prevention of Intravascular Catheter-Related Infections; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: CDC summary page dated February 28, 2024 and live-rechecked 2026-08-21; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: CDC Summary of Recommendations: Central Venous Catheters recommendation 10, line 60, promptly remove any intravascular catheter no longer essential; Hand Hygiene/Aseptic Technique lines 66-69; Maximal Sterile Barrier Precautions lines 72-78; Skin Preparation lines 79-87, including >0.5% chlorhexidine with alcohol for central venous catheter insertion when not contraindicated; Catheter Site Dressing Regimens line 95, no routine topical antibiotic ointment except dialysis catheters.
source_claim_supported: Current CDC HTML directly supports maximal sterile barriers for CVC/PICC insertion, appropriate chlorhexidine-alcohol skin preparation, aseptic catheter care, prompt removal when no longer essential, and avoidance of routine topical antibiotic ointment at ordinary insertion sites.
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: apply infection-prevention principles, protect clients from infection/injury, and use equipment safely.
pdf_visual_verification: PASS — the official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Safety and Infection Prevention and Control page was screenshot-verified earlier in this continuation; central-line claims are supported by current CDC HTML.

option_audit.A: Correct; all listed components are directly supported by current CDC recommendations.
option_audit.B: Plausible bundle format but includes routine topical antibiotic ointment and routine 24-hour CVC replacement, which are not supported prevention strategies.
option_audit.C: Plausible attempt to avoid reinsertion risk but conflicts with prompt removal when a catheter is no longer essential.
option_audit.D: Plausible partial bundle but omits maximal sterile barriers and adds unsupported routine 48-hour replacement.

cueing_audit.answer_length: Final alternatives are comparable in structure and detail; the correct option is not made conspicuous by letter position or a uniquely elaborate format.
cueing_audit.absolute_words: No distractor is rejected solely because of simplistic all/always/never wording.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified: B and D add unsupported routine replacement, C retains an unnecessary catheter, and D also omits maximal sterile barriers.
